learning_outcomes.text: The student will learn the most used purification techniques in organic chemistry, apply the knowledge acquired in Organic Chemistry I (acidity and basicity, reactivity of functional groups) and perform some simple laboratory experiments.

The student will become proficient in the use of the most common equipment in an organic chemistry laboratory. They will learn to reason about the reaction mechanism and to organize the procedure in each experiment.
The student will learn to respect basic safety rules in the laboratory, organize their work and compile a laboratory notebook.

syllabus_topics: Purification of a substance: crystallization, sublimation, solvent extraction (extraction of caffeine from tea)
Acidity and basicity (solubility in acidic or basic aqueous solutions)
Analysis of an unknown substance: solubility, crystallization, recognition of functional groups and their reactivity (preparation of the functional derivative)
Preparation of an azo dye (methyl orange and para red)
Synthesis and nitration reaction of methyl benzoate
teaching_methods: Introductory explanation before the laboratory experiment

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory notebook with reports on experiments performed
Oral exam discussing the laboratory experiments

assessment_rules: At the end of the course, students must submit the laboratory notebook with reports on the experiments performed. The oral exam will focus on the discussion of the laboratory experiences. The final grade, expressed out of thirty, considers the appropriateness, correctness, and coherence of knowledge, skills, and competencies, expressive ability, appropriate use of specific language, ability to connect different topics, synthesis ability, and critical spirit. Grades range from Sufficient (18-20/30) to Excellent (30), with honors attributed to candidates significantly above average. The exam is structured to highlight the achievement of competencies such as correlating chemical structure and physical properties, correlating structure and reactivity, and identifying reaction pathways.
